comparisonToTheMatchedFlashControl.note: the khal_deepseek-v4-flash matrix arm is the same recipe, the same suite, the same harness, at the same rlmx HEAD, and it ran CONCURRENTLY with this one (09:46:15-09:58:10 against 09:47:05-10:07:36), sharing the khal key and the three task roots. It is the matched control for this arm — contention, key and ground truth are all identical.
comparisonToTheMatchedFlashControl.consequence: qwen3.7-max is 4 facts BEHIND deepseek-v4-flash on the same recipe at 18.8x the round cost. Criteria 2 and 3 are clean on both, so this is a criterion-1 coverage gap, not a discipline failure.

comparisonToGen1sOwnRound.note: gen-1's recorded round is the same recipe and suite on flash, 84 minutes earlier and uncontended. Included because it is the number EVOLUTION.md carries, but the flash control above is the better comparison.
comparisonToGen1sOwnRound.caveat: the flash arm measured a +3-fact swing (29 -> 32) on an identical (recipe, model, suite) triple, so a 1-fact gap against gen-1 is inside run-to-run noise and carries no signal on its own. The 4-fact gap against the matched, concurrent flash control is at the edge of that measured band.

deviationsWorthReading: qwen3.7-max is the terser arm by a wide margin: 64 citations against the control's 109, and 381,511 input tokens against 841,504 — it reads less and says less. Its output tokens are HIGHER (177,164 vs 115,749) because the model emits reasoning tokens, which is also why the round costs 18.8x rather than the ~25x its input price alone implies.
every run stopped at 5-6 iterations of the 14 available, against the control's 5-14. No run was short of turns, so the coverage gap is not a budget effect.
the fan-out held: 17 spawns over 6 runs, 3 on every task except task 3 (2). This model does not skip the mandatory fan-out the way gen-2's prompt and the flash control's task 6 did.
task 3 F5 (npu_power.py:84) missed here as it has in every recorded round, gen-0 through gen-3 and in both matrix arms. It is the one fact no configuration has ever produced.
task 5 F5 (ptyManager.ts:127 RESERVED_ENV_KEYS) missed here. gen-1 and the flash control both hold it, so this is a model effect on the gen-1 prompt, not the gen-2/gen-3 prose regression.

consequenceRestated.original: qwen3.7-max is 4 facts BEHIND deepseek-v4-flash on the same recipe at 18.8x the round cost.
consequenceRestated.corrected: qwen3.7-max costs 18.8x more per round and 19-21x more per fact than deepseek-v4-flash on the same recipe, and is NOT measurably worse at finding facts. Against flash's corrected band the gap is +1 to +3 facts, inside the +/-3 run-to-run spread measured on flash itself (29 in gen-1's round, 32 in the matrix arm), and this arm is n=1 with no band measured at all.
consequenceRestated.costRankingIsRobust: flash $0.0047/fact published, $0.0048-$0.0052/fact across its band, against this arm's $0.1007/fact — a 19x-21x ratio that a +/-3-fact band moves by ~10%. The cost ordering of the four arms does not depend on the disputed fact counts.
consequenceRestated.winnerFraming: 'flash wins the matrix' is only defensible on cost. On facts the matrix is n=1 per arm and does not resolve an ordering between flash and qwen3.7-max. See matrix/README.md.
